rationale: The international study developed and validated the Parkinson Disease Pain Classification System. It distinguishes Parkinson-related pain from other pain and classifies mechanisms. No dried date exposure was recorded.

A nationwide retrospective comparison covered combinations of Parkinson stimulation and infusion therapies. Its tables include pain and abdominal pain among complications. These are device and medication comparisons with no dried-date dietary exposure.

The randomized Parkinson overactive-bladder trial compared pelvic floor muscle training and urge suppression with solifenacin. Pain or burning with urination appears in the adverse-event table. The study did not examine dried dates.

An open-label study tested a pharmaceutical NLRP3 inhibitor and measured exposure and inflammation markers. Reported adverse events included back pain in the treatment context. It had no date-fruit exposure.

The original protocol compares remote Baduanjin Qigong, conventional exercise rehabilitation and control for Parkinson symptoms and function. Quality-of-life and safety monitoring include bodily problems. This protocol gives no dried-date intervention or result.

The randomized 15-person crossover compared active and sham transcranial direct-current stimulation for Parkinson pain in relation to dopaminergic medication state. It directly measured pain but did not assign or record dried-date exposure as a comparison.

The clinical pilot tested transcranial random-noise stimulation for Parkinson mild cognitive impairment. It focused on cognitive measures and reported no culinary date exposure or dried-date pain comparison.

The study analyzed documented end-of-life preferences for Parkinson disease and atypical parkinsonism. It records treatment preferences and planning. It supplies no dietary exposure with a pain effect.
MOST-ABLE is a randomized protocol for oral semaglutide. The schedule includes appetite and broader Parkinson measures. It contains no dried-date comparison or completed pain result.

The randomized study added laughter yoga to Parkinson health education. It collected anxiety, depression and quality-of-life measures, including bodily discomfort as a PDQ-39 domain. It did not measure a dried-date exposure.

EMPOWER-PD evaluated a blended self-management program with goal setting and tracking. The symptom burden and wellness assessments concern the program. No dietary or dried date comparison was reported.
The sleep-disorder model identifies chronic pain as a covariate alongside mood measures, disease stage and levodopa-equivalent dose. It has no ingredient exposure or dried-date pain estimate.

The randomized comparison added robot-assisted arm training or recreation to Parkinson rehabilitation. The DASH scale and PDQ-39 bodily discomfort domain capture some symptom burden in that context. The trial reports no dried-date exposure.

The qualitative palliative-care study interviewed stakeholders about remote care for Parkinson disease. It addresses access and symptom-management needs. It reports no culinary date exposure or measured dried-date pain comparison.
The population-based wearable study compared motor measures, clinical characteristics and mortality in Parkinson disease. The study reports no dried date exposure or food-specific pain comparison.

The observational study examined sleep hygiene and sleep disturbance in early Parkinson disease. It recorded caffeine use and discussed pain among other contributors. It did not report dried date exposure or a food-specific pain estimate.

The original is a single-arm theta-burst stimulation feasibility protocol for depression in Lewy body dementia. Pain is mentioned in a tolerability rationale. It reports no intervention result or dried-date exposure.

The retrospective Parkinson study compared prediagnosis electronic records and prescription histories. Exposure was defined from recorded prescriptions. It reports no dried-date exposure paired with pain severity.

The retrospective comparison assessed perioperative nursing models in Parkinson deep brain stimulation. It records ambulation, length of stay, anxiety, depression and complications. It supplies no dietary intervention or dried-date pain result.
The acupuncture versus sham protocol specifies the King’s Parkinson’s Disease Pain Scale and prospective patient assessments. It reports no completed pain results and no dried-date exposure.

The VHIP cohort protocol schedules broad Parkinson symptom scales and a 14-item Mediterranean diet adherence screener. The screener records aggregate fruit servings without a dried-date item. The original reports no food-specific pain result.

The mixed-methods study examines hospital admission, length of stay, medication charting and readmission in Parkinson disease. Its interviews and outcomes address hospital care. It gives no date-fruit exposure or ingredient-specific pain estimate.
